description: Optional services fail visibly and independently: with no Gmail connection and no AI provider key, the Gmail send paths and AI dispatch answer a structured 503 {code:'provider_not_configured'} while every Release 0 money route still answers 2xx in the same app and environment. Run from apps/server: npx vitest run test/optional-services-fail-visibly.integration.test.ts src/modules/ai/model-gateway.service.spec.ts test/ai-direct-provider-503.integration.test.ts src/modules/ai/ai-usage.service.spec.ts src/modules/key-cortex/key-cortex-voice.service.spec.ts --reporter=json --outputFile=.proof/r0-07-vitest.json against a migrated local database and REDIS_URL, then node ../../scripts/proof-admission/evaluate.mjs --manifest ../../scripts/proof-admission/manifests/optional-services-fail-visibly.json --report .proof/r0-07-vitest.json. allowAdditionalCases is true only because model-gateway.service.spec.ts and ai-usage.service.spec.ts also carry pre-existing suites (58 and 52 cases these packets do not own); requireReportSuccess keeps every one of them binding. Follow-up R0-07a-AI-DIRECT-503 (COST-LEDGER-001 section 7 item 1) adds the AI calls that bypass the gateway: with neither AI_INTEGRATIONS_OPENAI_API_KEY nor OPENAI_API_KEY set, AiUsageService.trackEmbedding/trackVision/trackAudio and KeyCortexVoiceService answer the same 503 {code:'provider_not_configured', service:'ai'} before any OpenAI client, provider call, rate-limit slot, credit check or AiUsageLog row, and KEY voice builds no client with the sentinel key 'sk-no-key'; with a key (SDK resources or transport stubbed) behaviour is unchanged. RED-BEFORE for R0-07a (claude/elegant-curie-7azpsb at ab8efa35): POST /crm/businesses/:b/import/scan answered 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (the SDK constructor's OpenAIError), POST /voice/businesses/:b/tts attempted new OpenAI with no key, KEY voice built its client with 'sk-no-key' and POST /api/v1/cortex/voice/speak and /voice/listen sent .../audio/speech and .../audio/transcriptions with Authorization: Bearer sk-no-key (7 of 10 integration cases failed); 5 of 11 new ai-usage cases and 5 of 10 voice cases failed. Four it.todo cases in the R0-07a suite record routes whose 503 body code is lost, or whose error is swallowed, outside its write set (KeyCortexController speak/listen, OpenAiVoiceProvider and KeyflowVoiceService, CommerceVisionService, SemanticMemoryService); they are not required cases. R0-07a review ST-1 adds one integration case (a member of another business only, naming this business in the query, is refused 403 on the KEY voice routes before KEY voice runs; it passes on the unmodified code and is a negative control, not a fix) and one it.todo (speak and listen read @Query('businessId') while BusinessGuard checks params, then body, then query, so a JSON body businessId splits them; the fix, @GuardedBusinessId(), is in key-cortex.controller.ts, outside this write set; COST-LEDGER-001 section 7 item 9), which is not a required case. RED-BEFORE on the R0 working branch before this packet: the eight Gmail 503 cases answer 400 BAD_REQUEST ('Gmail not connected' / 'Google OAuth not configured'), the AI chat case answers 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, and three of the four gateway cases fail (plain Error; no code on the stream error chunk). Review repairs: ST-1 adds three gateway cases (a circuit belongs to the credential that failed, so one business's revoked BYOK key cannot make AI provider_unavailable for another business, RED-BEFORE: the other business got 503 provider_unavailable and its platform key was never tried) and ST-2 adds one integration case (a signed Gmail OAuth state is accepted once, RED-BEFORE: a replayed state was accepted). Three it.todo cases in the integration suite record review findings whose fix is outside this write set (ST-2 user binding, ST-3 auth-url guard, ST-4/R07-CR-1 web GET 503 retry); they are not required cases. Follow-up R0-CMF4-SEND-EMAIL-ORDER (COST-LEDGER-001 section 7 items 2 and 3) adds nine integration cases: a refused or failed send changes nothing. Quote send-email draws the view token of a DRAFT quote first and stores it, with the DRAFT -> SENT move and its quote.sent event, only after Gmail accepted the message; invoice send-email (CommerceService.sendWithPublicInvoiceUrl) reuses a live link as before and, when the invoice has none, writes the new PaymentLink (the token the email carried) only after Gmail accepted it. The order is send first, then write; no transaction or compensation. The cases run with no Gmail connection (503) and with a connected business whose real GmailService drives a stubbed Gmail transport that throws or answers an error (DRAFT quote stays DRAFT with no viewToken, no new PaymentLink, an existing live link is left as it was) or accepts the message (quote SENT with the emailed token, which opens it; exactly one live link whose token link is in the email and the response, D-07; a resend reuses it). RED-BEFORE on pkt/R0-21-WEB-PAYMENT-FORMS-repair (7435cb09; tests first at 913418a6): 4 of the 9 failed (the quote was left SENT with a viewToken, and a new PaymentLink row was left, both with no Gmail connection and with a failing transport). Fixture repair in the same commit: the PAID fixture now carries the SUCCESSFUL own-tenant payment that settles it; since V1-49 review (CR-V49-2) the required resend-receipt case answered 403 'Invoice is not yet paid' on that branch. R0-CMF4 review repairs (SEC-CMF4-1, SEC-CMF4-2, SEC-CMF4-3, CR-CMF4-1) add seven integration cases in which another request lands while the first send is with Gmail (a hook in the stubbed transport): the quote's view token is reserved on the DRAFT before the send by a compare-and-set and cleared when Gmail did not accept the message, and the DRAFT -> SENT move after an accepted send is a compare-and-set (updateQuoteStatus ifStatus), so an operator rejection made meanwhile is kept (409 quote_changed_during_send with emailSent, no quote.sent, the emailed link cannot accept it), and a second click or a 'mark sent' leaves every emailed link opening the quote with one quote.sent event and contact event; an invoice with no live link gets its PaymentLink before the send with a pending expiry that every other hand-out claims (reissueLink), so a second send-email shares the one live link (revoking it closes both emails), an accepted send leaves it with no expiry, and a failed first send removes it only while no other request has handed it out. RED-BEFORE on pkt/R0-CMF4-SEND-EMAIL-ORDER (022f0604): 6 of the 7 failed (the seventh, the hook-and-outbound check, is a harness invariant). The order is no longer 'send first, then write' with no compensation: the reservation is written first and removed on failure.
